metadata.label: PIONIER image, November 2016
metadata.coverage: The published SQUEEZE reconstruction of Montargès et al. (2018, A&A 614, A12) for November 2016, deposited at the CDS as a 32 by 32 pixel image of 0.5 milliarcseconds, cast onto a sphere of the limb-darkened diameter at the Gaia distance. The camera is computed: the star has no measured rotation axis, so the display axis is celestial north in the plane of the sky, the display meridian is the sub-Earth point at the epoch, and the pixel scale is the image's. The image is shown as its authors published it, at a pixel scale finer than the 1.8 milliarcsecond beam of the longest baseline; its features are the authors' reconstruction. The colours are a legend for reconstructed relative intensity in the H band, not colour or temperature. The far hemisphere is unobserved.

reconstruction.filter: H band 1.51-1.77 um, six channels merged by the authors

transfer.interpretation: Trial acceptance bounds, not estimates of source accuracy. A footprint is the pixel's range times its angular size, 49 million kilometres at the disc centre from 658 parsecs, so a contributor lies within two of those of the closest sphere point; the one-metre visibility tolerance is numerically zero on a body this size, and the sphere is convex, so no point occludes another.

science.qualification: Uniform photosphere colour from the star's Crimean photoelectric spectrum. The disc is unresolved: no map, limb darkening or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

offLimbContext.source: the same published image: its light outside the 10.18 mas disc on the lens palette and stretch with alpha fading to the background; the plate spans the 16 mas field
offLimbContext.composition: sky-plane image registered to the disc (496 px = 10.18 mas), mirrored and turned to the scene's handedness so its north meets the rendered display axis at the default camera
offLimbContext.rotation: stationary sky-plane context; drawn behind the sphere, so the disc itself is hidden

limbMaterial.composition: transparent: the sphere's own silhouette is the limb; the light just outside it is on the off-limb plate
